sec: Acinar zones, vitelline vein fates and the lobe division lines

items.q: Match each zone label in the figure with the injury it is arrowed to — 1) Periportal 2) Mid-zonal 3) Centrilobular … A) Ischemic hepatitis and paracetamol positioning B) Involved in Wilson's disease C) Yellow phosphorous positioning, printed as RATOL position
items.exp: Three arrows leave the zone brackets, the periportal one pointing to Wilson's disease, the mid-zonal one straight down to the yellow phosphorous line and the centrilobular one down to the two bullets for ischemic hepatitis and paracetamol. (Book p984)

items.q: All of the following zone to injury pairings are drawn on this page EXCEPT:
items.exp: Paracetamol is bullet-marked at the centrilobular end together with ischemic hepatitis, so pairing it with the periportal zone contradicts the arrows of the figure. (Book p984)

items.q: Which zone number is printed directly above the bracket that the yellow phosphorous arrow points to?
items.exp: The hepatocyte row is numbered ZONE 1 under the periportal span, ZONE 2 under mid-zonal and ZONE 3 under centrilobular, and the yellow phosphorous line hangs below the ZONE 2 bracket. (Book p984)

items.q: Assess the two bracket statements in the figure: I The portal tract bracket ends where the periportal span begins and the parenchyma bracket runs to the terminal hepatic vein. II The three structures grouped under the peripheral bracket are hepatic artery, bile duct and portal vein.
items.exp: The lower double arrow labelled portal tract covers the triad of hepatic artery, bile duct and portal vein, and the second double arrow labelled parenchyma extends from the septal vein region to the terminal hepatic vein. (Book p984)

items.q: Fill up: The channel drawn leaving the hepatocyte plate and entering the bile duct of the portal tract is labelled the canal of ______, and the crossing vessel near it is the ______ vein.
items.exp: The figure's internal labels are Canal of Hering for the ductule at the edge of the parenchyma, Septal vein for the crossed vessel, plus Arteriole below the hepatic artery. (Book p984)

items.q: Match each vitelline vein segment with its fate on the flow chart — 1) Right superior 2) Right inferior 3) Left inferior 4) Left superior … A) Regresses B) Portal vein C) Common hepatic vein
items.exp: Under Right, the superior branch descends to the common hepatic vein and the inferior to the portal vein, while under Left the inferior also joins the portal vein and the superior simply regresses. (Book p984)

items.q: Assess the two vitelline statements: I The portal vein is a single midline structure formed from the inferior segments of both vitelline veins. II The left superior vitelline vein persists as the terminal hepatic vein.
items.exp: Both inferior limbs funnel into Portal vein in the centre of the chart, whereas the left superior limb ends in Regresses, the common hepatic vein being the fate of the right superior limb. (Book p984)

items.q: Where is the falciform ligament placed, and what does the page say it divides?
opts: On the anterior surface, separating the left and right lobes
On the posterior surface, separating the caudate and quadrate lobes
On the inferior surface, separating the right lobe from the caudate
Along the right coronary ligament, separating bare area from dome
items.exp: The two bullets for the falciform ligament read anterior surface and anatomically divides liver lobes into left and right. (Book p984)

items.q: Fill up: Cantlie's line is drawn as an imaginary line running from the ______ to the ______.
opts: gall bladder fossa; inferior vena cava
items.exp: The line is defined as imaginary, running from the gall bladder fossa, printed in red, to the inferior vena cava, also in red, and it divides the liver into left and right parts. (Book p984)

items.q: Every statement below fits Cantlie's line as written EXCEPT:
opts: It is a peritoneal fold on the anterior surface
It runs to the inferior vena cava
It divides the liver into left and right parts
items.exp: Being a peritoneal fold on the anterior surface is the description of the falciform ligament, the entry immediately above Cantlie's line, which shares with it only the left and right division. (Book p984)

items.q: A 30-year-old is brought in 72 hours after a massive paracetamol ingestion and a biopsy is taken. According to the zone arrows on this page, where will necrosis be heaviest?
opts: Epithelium of the canal of Hering
items.exp: Paracetamol positioning is one of the two bullets hanging off the centrilobular bracket, with ischemic hepatitis, so the zone 3 parenchyma around the terminal hepatic vein is the site. (Book p984)

items.q: A worker inhaling fumes in a matches and fireworks plant develops acute hepatotoxicity from yellow phosphorous. Which band of the lobule does this page assign to that toxin?
items.exp: The arrow from the mid-zonal bracket points at the yellow phosphorous line with its RATOL parenthetical, distinct from the Wilson's arrow on one side and the paracetamol bullets on the other. (Book p984)

items.q: Which labelled vessel stands at the far right of the lobule figure, receiving the centrilobular end of the parenchyma bracket?
items.exp: The label at the centre of the figure is Terminal hepatic vein, sitting under a bracket headed Center, exactly where the parenchyma arrow ends. (Book p984)

items.q: Assess the two histology captions: I The micrographs on this page are captioned histology of simple hepatic acini. II The Wilson's disease arrow is aimed at the periportal zone because copper accumulates first around the terminal hepatic vein.
items.exp: The caption beneath the two stained plates reads histology of simple hepatic acini, and the Wilson's arrow belongs to the periportal end, so any centrilobular reasoning is the opposite of what is shown. (Book p984)
